Summary: ss CLI re-parses argv into a pwsh command line so a multi-word Summary or EosLog body is re-tokenized on spaces and breaks on parenthesis or semicolon characters, which blocks external callers from filing Requests with normal prose

EosLog.Disposition: filed via the workaround it documents
EosLog.Body: Repro from an external shell, call ss.exe with Remedy-ChangeRequest and a quoted multi-word Summary. The quotes are lost when ss joins argv into one string and re-parses it as a pwsh command line, so only the first word binds to Summary and the rest fail as extra positional parameters. Parenthesis and semicolon characters anywhere in the Summary or in an Add-EosLog body get evaluated by that re-parse and error. Impact, no external caller including Claude can file a Request or EOS log with normal prose, so the 2026-06-22 session handoff went to ss-log.md instead of the hive. Fix direction, on verb dispatch pass the original argv array straight to the cmdlet binder rather than rejoining argv into a string and re-tokenizing, or quote-escape each argv element before the rejoin. Current workaround, wrap each multi-word arg in literal double quotes.

EosLog.Disposition: Confirmed live and still open - fresh repro from the audit session 2026-06-23
EosLog.Body: Re-hit INC105 first-hand while filing CRQ136. ss.exe Remedy-ChangeRequest with a normal-prose Summary failed: ss: At line:1 char:665 Missing argument in parameter list - ss.exe reconstructed the argv into a pwsh command line and broke on a parenthesis and a -A token embedded in the prose. The path that SUCCEEDED: file via the MCP ss_run runspace with a single-quoted pwsh string, which binds -Summary as a literal and never re-tokenizes. So the runspace cmdlet surface is usable for prose but the ss.exe CLI is not. Confirms INC105 is load-bearing for any external caller filing Requests. Cleanest fix: have ss.exe bind argv straight to the cmdlet parameters instead of joining argv and re-parsing as a script line.

Canonize the boundary taxonomy DpBoundary / VomBoundary. A foreign engine the system cannot mesh is owned at the near side by ONE primitive - VomBoundary held by a VOM handle (control, request/response, ordered) - DpBoundary streamed through a DirectPort port (data, push/fenced/latest-wins). An engine = one VomBoundary plus N DpBoundaries = the control/data-plane split from the drop test. Gradient VOM-in-proc then DpBoundary then VomBoundary then unmanaged=drift. Closed pair by design (2 primitives) - mechanism words process/runspace/machine-boundary stay plain English, orthogonal. Add to docs/CONTRACT.md, add the or-a-declared-boundary branch to the coherence test, file an SSxxx analyzer requiring every foreign interop (P/Invoke, COM, child process, embedded blob) to be a declared boundary - undeclared foreign = drift. Scott 2026-06-25 ratified DpBoundary/VomBoundary.
